text:
Evan Rodrigues scored in overtime on Saturday to beat the Islanders, finishing a breakaway that Anthony Mantha's pass created. It was his third goal of the season and a reminder why New Jersey brought in a two-time Cup winner from Florida: he fits wherever you put him.

The numbers are mixed. His own finishing is a touch ahead of schedule, 3 goals on 2.39 expected. But New Jersey, a team taking 59% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) overall, is more than ten points worse in that share with him on the ice. Some of that is deployment on a deep team, and some is luck: the Devils have scored 7.0 fewer goals than their chances deserve with him out there, which has cost him points.

He's 33, undrafted, and Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking from last season shows a clean puck mover: 64% of his exits leave the zone with possession. He shoots a lot but not from the slot. We project about 35 points. On a 12-5 team, that's a useful middle-six piece. He missed time with an illness early this month, so watch his minutes settle back in.
headline: Rodrigues is quietly doing fine
